Agent-Based Model activity diagram For example, agent-based models (ABM) represent an approach with which to investigate the adoption of MDHD electric vehicles.108 ABMs particularly allow for bottom-up modeling of complex systems that involve social dynamics. The traditional challenge in developing ABMs for adoption modeling has been assigning weighting and importance to the multiplicity of considerations that adopters will take into account in making a purchase decision. An ABM model of MDHD EV adoption would ask the purchasing agent to simultaneously consider the influence of long-term costs, policy/incentives, the suitability of the technology to their application, their perception of the reliability of the technology, and so on [37]. Traditionally, the relative importance of these simultaneous considerations has been assessed via survey. The START methods presented above now give us data-driven means to weigh the importance of these simultaneous considerations of MDHD EV adopters. As a demonstration, the rankings from Figure 40 are implemented in the ABM designed by Trinko to model MDHD EV adoption, using the procedure documented in Figure 41. Figure 42 shows the differences between the average number of EVs purchased each year across three fleet managers. The figure shows that using adoption perceptions held in academic literature leads to a prediction of much earlier, and faster, adoption of MDHD EVs while the use of industry perceptions forecasts a 10-year delay in increased EV purchases by MDHD fleet managers. 108 Bankes SC. Agent-based model results with different perception weights Conclusions The lack of data in the field of MDHD EV adoption perceptions leaves members of this field, both in academia and industry, with a blurred understanding of why this process is going slower than light-duty EV adoption. Our work helps to clarify this understanding by introducing a comprehensive metric, START, that combines results from a traditional statistical approach, LDA, and another, more cutting-edge, machine learning model, BERTopic. START allows us to provide actionable insights to industry and academics alike. Professionals can use these results to make more informed decisions based on the information distilled from the text that their industry produces, and academic researchers can use the same information to help guide their research in directions relevant to the needs of industry.
